items.title: As the school year settles in, making room for the arts can support everyday well‑being
items.summary: As the days darken, making more room for arts-based practices and experiences is one way to bring useful, interesting or sustaining activities into the seasons ahead.

items.title: Ball or strike? Why the count may change what a baseball umpire sees
items.summary: In baseball, a borderline pitch is more likely to be called a strike when the batter has three balls and no strikes than when the count is no balls and two strikes. The official strike zone hasn't changed. The umpire's judgment has.

items.title: AI platform and database map protein phase separation across species

items.title: Why a tiny number of venture capitalists capture almost all the profit
items.summary: Beyond a handful of big names, most venture capitalists are relatively unknown. Who are they, and what distinguishes the superstars from the rest?

items.title: Climate fingerprints reveal stronger evidence of human-caused warming after more than 30 years
items.summary: The scientific evidence for human-caused global warming is stronger than ever, according to a major new review—despite a U.S. government report questioning the science.

items.title: DNA reveals genetic divide in Australian brolgas, with southern birds facing greater diversity risks
items.summary: New research on the brolga, an iconic Australian crane species, has shown important genetic differences between northern and southeastern populations, with evidence that those in western Victoria are at increased risk, likely heightened by the loss of wetlands.

items.title: Why some anglers always follow the rules
items.summary: New research sheds light on why a surprising number of fishers always follow fishing rules, even when enforcement is unlikely and breaking the rules offers a financial reward.

items.title: New sensor uses slowed light to detect gravitational pull of tiny objects
items.summary: Gravity, the attraction between objects with mass, is the weakest of the four fundamental forces governing physical processes. Detecting the tiny gravitational pull of objects that are just a few millimeters in size and have a very small mass is extremely challenging.

items.title: Study explores why Indigenous communities may accept oil extraction despite its harms
items.summary: The uneven distribution of oil extraction's impacts and benefits helps explain why some Indigenous communities accept it, newly published research shows.

items.title: Model links course design, psychological safety and guided AI use
items.summary: University of Phoenix researchers have published a new peer-reviewed study examining how stress, self-regulation, resilience, belonging, psychological safety and generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) interact in the experiences of nontraditional online students. items.title: Americans Hall and Woodford win economics Nobel for stabilization models
items.summary: Americans Robert Hall and Michael Woodford were awarded the Nobel economics prize Monday for their work on how monetary and fiscal policy can better stabilize disruptive economic fluctuations.

items.title: AI platforms offer promise in limiting the illegal wildlife trade
items.summary: New University of Kent research has found promising signs that AI platforms have the potential to limit the illegal wildlife trade. The research paper titled "Assessing safeguards against the illegal wildlife trade on AI platforms" is published in Conservation Biology.

items.title: Hybrid quantum computers could finally get to grips with light and matter
items.summary: Many of nature's most important processes depend on how particles of matter interact with light and other force-carrying particles. So far, however, it has proven difficult for conventional computers to determine how individual particles behave in these interactions.

items.summary: Popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs, such as Ozempic and Wegovy, have been linked to unexpectedly high rates of nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation, with some problems occurring several times more frequently among users. items.title: Scientists find hidden driver of aging and a simple amino acid that fights memory loss in mice
items.summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of a protein called Menin may help drive aging, and restoring it in older mice reversed several age-related changes in just 30 days. items.title: Hurricane Simon churns off Mexican coast after shift in course
items.summary: Hurricane Simon shifted track slightly on Sunday and was forecast to skirt Mexico's west coast without making landfall, while packing heavy rain and severe winds.

items.title: World leaders urged to 'course correct' as UN nature goals fall short
items.summary: Nations are steeling for a disappointing report card at this month's U.N. biodiversity summit, with governments falling short on their commitments to protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.

items.title: El Niño sets temperature record in key Pacific zone: EU monitor
items.summary: An intensifying El Niño broke a temperature record in a key zone of the Pacific in September, the EU's climate monitor said Monday, in another sign the weather pattern is gaining exceptional strength.

items.title: Italian rice farmer beats heat with biodiversity haven
items.summary: Four hundred years after monks transformed a patch of marshlands in northwest Italy into rice fields, farmer Alice Cerutti has restored a third to their natural state, prioritizing biodiversity over crop yield.

items.title: NASA captures a stunning transformation in Australia's red outback
items.summary: Australia's normally dry, rust-colored outback has erupted into a spectacular carpet of wildflowers after unusually heavy rains, potentially producing its most impressive bloom in nearly 20 years. items.summary: The ice reached its third-lowest maximum extent since satellite observations began.

items.summary: Getting better sleep might be as simple as moving a little more every day. items.summary: Wildlife populations around the world have declined by an average of 73% since 1970. items.summary: Scientists have succeeded in reconstructing the family tree of cells in a developing mouse embryo. items.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising secret behind a mushroom disease that has frustrated growers for more than a century: It involves more than 17 species of harmful bacteria, not just one. items.summary: Mathematics may hold unexpected clues to understanding Alzheimer’s disease. items.title: Quantum 'birthmarks' hold lasting traces of a system's past
items.summary: Some classical physical systems can explore many configurations over time until their long-term behavior no longer reveals their starting conditions. The sampling of available configurations according to the appropriate statistical distribution is a property called ergodicity.

items.title: New study shows effects of hypoxia in Florida's Banana River
items.summary: A new study by Florida Tech assistant professor of marine sciences Austin Fox, Ph.D. '15, found that low oxygen levels are contributing to the rerelease of nutrients buried on the river floor that feed harmful algal blooms. items.title: Conservation groups alarmed at marine mammals' deaths in Spain
items.summary: Conservation groups on Sunday condemned the death of a dolphin transferred from France to a Spanish marine park, saying it added to the deaths of other sea mammals recently moved to Spain from Canada.

items.title: Indonesia releases eight orangutans rescued from fires to protected forest
items.summary: Eight orangutans rescued in recent weeks from blazes that tore through Borneo island have been released into a protected forest, Indonesian authorities and rescuers said on Sunday.

items.title: Scientists make stunning discovery that could help explain why life exists
items.summary: Scientists have discovered that the universe's fundamental physical constants may be finely balanced to make life possible. items.title: At least 4 dead as cyclone Isaias drenches southern U.S.
items.summary: Four people died in the southeastern United States as post-tropical cyclone Isaias posed flooding and tornado risks Saturday as it moved northward after making landfall on Florida's Gulf Coast.

items.title: Jurassic fossil reveals ancient origins of how mammals drink milk
items.summary: An international team of researchers has uncovered new evidence illuminating the evolutionary origins of one of the defining features of mammals: the ability to suckle and consume milk during infancy. items.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens as it nears western Mexico
items.summary: Hurricane Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm and was expected to make landfall or skirt the coast of west-central Mexico on Sunday, according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center.

items.title: South Korea completes trial of Arctic shipping route
items.summary: A South Korean container ship returned on Sunday from a trial voyage through the Arctic, testing an alternative route opened by melting sea ice as conflict in the Middle East disrupts global shipping.

items.title: Egypt's Fayoum mummy portraits to travel abroad for first time after restoration
items.summary: Egypt unveiled Sunday a restored version of the "Tondo of the Two Brothers," a prized second-century painting from the famed Fayoum portraits.
